Are a strong systems thinker who can connect user experiences to the underlying platform, business logic, and technical architecture.
Have experience designing complex, infrastructure-adjacent, platform, or enterprise product experiences.
Have strong UX/UI and interaction design skills, with a high bar for quality, clarity, and craft.
Are comfortable leading an ambiguous product area, developing a clear vision, and shaping a roadmap alongside product and engineering partners.
Can explain complex decisions and tradeoffs clearly to technical, business, and design stakeholders.
Enjoy solving problems where scalability, reliability, and long-term product coherence matter as much as the immediate user experience.
Are excited by defining how customers understand and pay for emerging AI products and behaviors.
Have experience with payments, billing, pricing, monetization, or usage-based products, or are eager to apply strong platform-design experience to those challenges.
Can work within, improve, and contribute to a shared design system.

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. The Design Systems team creates the foundations that help teams across OpenAI build coherent, high-quality experiences at scale.
Accessibility is fundamental to that work. We’re building the shared standards, components, tools, and practices that make inclusive experiences the default across OpenAI’s products and platforms.

In this role, you’ll lead OpenAI’s company-wide accessibility program from within Design Foundations. You’ll pair strategy and organizational influence with hands-on product design—advocating for disabled people, removing barriers across complete customer journeys, and establishing durable ownership throughout the company.
This is an opportunity to define accessibility for a new generation of products spanning web, mobile, desktop, voice, AI, and hardware. You’ll help teams consider the many ways people perceive, understand, navigate, and interact with technology, going beyond minimum compliance to create experiences that are genuinely useful and inclusive.
Working across design, engineering, research, product, go-to-market, and legal, you’ll make accessibility an expected part of product quality—not a final review or the responsibility of a single expert.
This role is based in our San Francisco HQ. We offer relocation assistance to new employees.

Define OpenAI’s accessibility strategy, roadmap, governance, priorities, and measures of progress.
Design and ship accessible experiences while identifying systemic barriers across complete customer journeys.
Build accessibility into our design system through inclusive components, tokens, interaction patterns, Figma libraries, documentation, and engineering guardrails.
Center disabled people through participatory research, usability studies, and assistive-technology testing rather than relying solely on assumptions, simulations, or automated tools.
Design for permanent, temporary, and situational disabilities, including multiple ways to perceive information, navigate interfaces, understand content, and complete important tasks.
Establish practical standards for screen readers, keyboard navigation, focus, reading order, contrast, typography, motion, captions, forms, errors, and multimodal interactions.
Lead accessibility audits, remediation priorities, launch readiness, and continuous validation across platforms.
Partner with go-to-market, legal, compliance, and product teams on enterprise readiness, accessibility documentation, procurement needs, and customer commitments.
Grow company-wide capability through training, critiques, engineering partnerships, and a network of accessibility champions.

s.h: You might thrive in this role if you

Pair deep accessibility expertise with strong interaction design, systems thinking, and a high bar for product craft.
Understand the relationship between accessibility, usability, and inclusive design—and know when to go beyond standards to meet real human needs.
Have deep practical knowledge of WCAG, assistive technologies, accessible interaction design, and platform-specific standards.
Have embedded accessibility into design systems, reusable components, and engineering workflows.
Have worked directly with disabled people and translated their experiences into meaningful product and organizational decisions.
Can identify assumptions and exclusion within a product journey, then turn those insights into clearer and more flexible ways to interact.
Are equally effective setting strategy, designing detailed experiences, and collaborating with engineers through implementation.
Can influence across disciplines without direct authority, creating shared accountability without becoming a centralized approval gate.

Synthesia is the world’s leading AI video platform for business, used by over 90% of the Fortune 100. Founded in 2017, the company is headquartered in London, with offices and teams across Europe and the US.
As AI continues to shape the way we live and work, Synthesia develops products to enhance visual communication and enterprise skill development, helping people work better and stay at the center of successful organizations.
Following our recent Series E funding round, where we raised $200 million, our valuation stands at $4 billion. Our total funding exceeds $530 million from premier investors including Accel, NVentures (Nvidia's VC arm), Kleiner Perkins, GV, and Evantic Capital, alongside the founders and operators of Stripe, Datadog, Miro, and Webflow.
Location: Europe remote or London hybrid

Synthesia is used by over 90% of the Fortune 100. The largest deployments now run thousands of creators across dozens of markets, languages, and compliance regimes. What decides whether those accounts expand or stall is not another avatar - it's whether admins, legal teams, and programme owners can actually stay in control.
We're looking for a Staff (L6) Product Designer to own that layer end-to-end: workspace setup and governance, the content lifecycle, and the analytics and integrations that close the loop. This is the work that turns a proof of concept into a seven-figure renewal, and right now it is wide open.
You'll operate as a senior IC: setting direction, influencing roadmap decisions (not just contributing), shaping bets with Product and Engineering leaders, and raising the bar on how we think about enterprise design problems.

Own the Enterprise surface end-to-end, from problem framing to shipped outcomes and iteration - often dealing with ambiguity. You'll reach out to the right stakeholders, get the right eyes in the room, and make decisions independently.
Design complex governance and compliance systems that give admins, legal teams, and compliance officers genuine control and transparency. Examples include:
Permission models and role hierarchies that scale across thousands of creators without collapsing into chaos.
Audit log experiences that make compliance auditable - not just for the system, but for the humans who need to understand what happened.
Workspace setup and identity workflows that integrate with real enterprise infrastructure (SSO, SCIM, MCP).
License and billing models that admins can actually understand and manage at scale.
Analytics and reporting that tell admins whether their deployment is working as intended.
Work with technical constraints and possibilities . You'll develop fluency in APIs, widget architectures, developer hub patterns, and how backend systems shape what's actually achievable in the UX. You're not designing in isolation from engineering - you're designing in partnership with it.
Drive pragmatic iteration . You'll scope ruthlessly, build POCs to get signal early, and iterate based on what you learn from enterprise customers.
Set a design vision for our Enterprise surface and influence adjacent product areas to stay coherent. As things scale across SSO, compliance, analytics, and billing, you're keeping the mental model consistent.

s.h: You should apply if you bring
s.t:
Significant experience designing complex, large-scale product surfaces - ideally admin dashboards, governance layers, analytics platforms, or other domains where system thinking matters.
Technical fluency. You understand APIs, integrations, how services communicate, how widgets and developer hubs work. You can read a technical architecture doc and understand the constraints it creates for design. You don't need to be an engineer, but you think like one.
Systems thinking: not just about interaction flows, but about enterprise systems. You understand how identity systems, compliance regimes, and scale constraints shape what's actually possible in the UX. You think in mental models and multi-step workflows, not single screens.
Comfort operating in ambiguity: you can turn unclear and fast-moving problem spaces into crisp direction, and you do not wait for perfect clarity.
Excellent communication in design reviews and cross-functional decision-making contexts.
Experience designing workflows where trust, transparency, and user control are central - helping users feel confident in AI-driven outputs rather than confused or excluded.
The ability to leverage feedback from users and customers to ensure the product continues to meet real needs - including enterprise users with high stakes around quality, compliance, and scale.

At Vanta, our mission is to help businesses earn and prove trust. We believe that security should be monitored and verified continuously, and we empower companies to practice better security and prove it with ease. Vanta has a kind and talented team, and while some have prior security experience, many have been successful at Vanta without it.
The Design Systems team creates the visual and interaction foundations that help Vanta deliver coherent, accessible, and high-quality experiences across the product. This team partners across the EPD organization to build the systems, patterns, and practices that enable product teams to move faster while maintaining a high bar for craft and usability.
As a Staff Visual Product Designer focused on Design Systems at Vanta, you will shape the visual language of our product and the systems that bring it to life.

You will define and evolve scalable patterns across our design and engineering ecosystems, partner closely with product designers and engineers, and help create a cohesive experience for customers navigating complex security and compliance workflows.

You’ll combine exceptional visual craft with systems thinking, product judgment, and the ability to influence across teams.
What you’ll do as a Staff Visual Product Designer, Design Systems at Vanta:
Define and evolve Vanta’s visual design language across product surfaces, creating a cohesive, distinctive, and scalable customer experience.
Set a high bar for visual craft across typography, color, layout, iconography, illustration, motion, data visualization, and interaction details.
Partner with Design Systems, Product, Engineering, Research, Content Design, and Brand teams to translate customer and business needs into effective system-level solutions.
Own and evolve foundational design system elements, including design tokens, component visual states, responsive behavior, theming, density, and platform-specific adaptations.
Create reusable patterns and guidance that help product teams solve common problems consistently while preserving flexibility for different customer workflows.
Design and prototype system components and end-to-end product experiences, using high-fidelity exploration to communicate intent and accelerate alignment.
Bring visual clarity and hierarchy to complex, data-rich workflows used by security, compliance, IT, legal, finance, and business stakeholders.
Collaborate with engineers to ensure designs are implemented with fidelity, accessibility, performance, and maintainability in mind.
Establish principles, standards, and review practices that raise the quality and consistency of product design across Vanta.
Advocate for inclusive and accessible visual design, ensuring that color, contrast, typography, motion, and interaction states work for a broad range of users and contexts.
Help define how the design system supports emerging product needs, including AI-powered experiences, personalization, automation, and increasingly complex enterprise workflows.
Use customer insights, product data, usability feedback, and competitive research to identify opportunities to improve the system and its impact.
Working AI-natively: uses AI tools throughout the design process, and has shipped designs for non-deterministic, AI-powered experiences (chat, agentic modalities, etc).
Facilitate critiques, workshops, and cross-functional reviews that help teams make stronger visual and product decisions.
Influence product strategy and roadmap decisions through strong design perspectives, compelling narratives, prototypes, and a clear point of view.
Mentor product designers and contribute to a culture of thoughtful critique, continuous learning, experimentation, and customer obsession.
Create documentation, examples, and enablement materials that make the design system easy to understand, adopt, and extend.
Define and measure the impact of the design system through adoption, consistency, accessibility, usability, delivery efficiency, and customer outcomes.
Represent Design Systems in planning processes, product reviews, and other cross-functional forums, helping teams align around a shared vision for the Vanta experience.
Contribute to the broader Design organization by sharing best practices, strengthening design craft, and improving how Vanta approaches visual product quality.

s.h: How to be successful in this role
s.t:
8+ years of experience designing digital products, with significant experience in visual product design for complex B2B SaaS or enterprise software.
Deep expertise in visual design for digital products, including typography, color, composition, layout, iconography, illustration, motion, interaction states, and data visualization.
A strong portfolio demonstrating exceptional visual craft, thoughtful systems thinking, and the ability to improve product experiences at both the component and end-to-end workflow level.
Experience creating, evolving, and scaling product design systems used by multiple teams across a growing organization.
Strong understanding of design tokens, component architecture, responsive design, accessibility, and the relationship between design tools and front-end implementation.
A track record of turning ambiguous product and customer problems into clear, elegant, and reusable visual solutions.
Experience partnering closely with engineers to bring detailed visual designs to life and to make pragmatic decisions when implementation constraints arise.
Strong product thinking, with the ability to understand customer needs, business goals, technical constraints, and the broader relationships among product surfaces and workflows.
Excellent communication, storytelling, and facilitation skills, with the ability to influence product and engineering partners without relying on formal authority.
Experience balancing consistency and flexibility, knowing when to use an existing pattern, when to extend it, and when to introduce something new.
A demonstrated ability to give and receive thoughtful feedback, mentor others, and raise the quality bar across a design organization.
Comfortable operating in ambiguity, making decisions with incomplete information, and balancing strategic thinking with a bias for action.
Experience designing products in cybersecurity, compliance, GRC, IT, infrastructure, financial services, or another complex and regulated domain is a plus.
Experience with tools such as Figma and familiarity with front-end technologies or design system implementation workflows is a plus.
A strong commitment to Vanta’s principles: putting customers first, biasing for action, winning as one team, deciding with frameworks, leading with resilience, and doing what it says on the tin.
Required: Bachelor’s degree in Design, Human-Computer Interaction, Psychology, Computer Science, or a related field.
Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for current or future employer sponsorship.
Responsible for protecting Vanta and customer data in how you operate and deliver results.
Open to using AI to amplify their skills and strengthen their work - demonstrating curiosity, a willingness to learn, and sound judgment in applying AI responsibly to improve efficiency and impact.

At Vanta, our mission is to help businesses earn and prove trust. Lead end-to-end design for projects across the agent harness, from problem framing and discovery through launch and iteration.
Define how agents, skills, tools, and memory are composed, surfaced, and understood by customers.
Design experiences that help customers delegate real security and compliance work while maintaining visibility, control, and confidence.
Create patterns for reviewing, correcting, approving, interrupting, and recovering from agent-generated work.

Translate customer insights, product requirements, technical constraints, and AI quality considerations into clear design direction.

Create design briefs, workflow models, prototypes, specifications, and other artifacts that bring clarity to complex problems.
Communicate design rationale, tradeoffs, risks, and recommendations clearly to cross-functional partners and leadership.
Contribute to design critique and help raise the quality bar for interaction design, information architecture, UX writing, and visual craft.
Help shape how Vanta approaches responsible AI and human control across the product.
Identify opportunities to improve how the design organization and product teams work together.

Experience designing products that require human judgment, including deciding when and how to bring a person into an automated workflow.

Strong product thinking and discovery skills, including the ability to frame ambiguous problems and identify the right questions to answer.

Strong cross-functional collaboration skills, particularly with Product, Engineering, Research, Data, and customer-facing teams.

A portfolio that demonstrates shipped work, complex workflows, meaningful tradeoffs, and learning from customers or users.
Ability to move fluidly between systems-level thinking and detailed interaction design.
Clear communication skills and the ability to influence cross-functional partners without formal authority.

We need a designer who finds that reality energizing, someone who brings the same rigor, curiosity, and care to every product they touch, whatever the audience.

Product and UX/UI Design
Design products and features end to end, from initial concept through launch and ongoing improvement, for tools that directly impact Chartis consulting teams and their clients.
Take messy, real-world workflows and turn them into interfaces that are clear, efficient, and trustworthy, no matter how complicated the systems behind them are.
Design for AI-assisted workflows, including surfaces where users interpret model outputs, review recommendations, and collaborate alongside AI and human teammates to carry out their consulting work.
Conduct user research with stakeholders to ground design decisions in real work context.
Work with product managers and engineers to understand how AI models actually behave, including where it falls short, so you can design interfaces that set the right expectations and build trust.
Collaborate closely with engineering to ensure design intent carries through implementation, and advocate for quality and the best user experience when tradeoffs are proposed.
Design Systems and Standards
Contribute to and help maintain a design system that serves multiple products and can evolve as the product landscape changes.

Help drive product strategy and roadmap decisions, bringing a clear, evidence-based user perspective and pushing for the right priorities, not just responding to them.
Turn research, prototypes, and design rationale into narratives and visuals that make the impact of the work legible to non-designers, building the buy-in needed to move decisions forward.
Lead design reviews, document decisions clearly, and help raise the bar for product and user experience.

0-to-1 design systems: you’ve built entire design systems and component libraries from scratch, not just worked within one that already existed.

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

Prompts spec out what Claude does. Evals measure whether it did. The Product Prompt and Eval Design team does both for product design: the system prompt that greets a new user, the tool descriptions that decide whether Claude searches, the instructions that keep a slide deck from tipping into slop, and the evals that test all of it.

The point is to keep the model and the product aligned with what users expect, what the product strategy calls for, and what safety requires, on every surface and through every model launch.
This role is a foundational member of that work on the eval side: building the evals that check the prompts, the harness that runs them, and the tools that let designers do this work themselves. It sits on the Product Prompt and Eval Design team in Product Design, works day to day with the team's surface owners and the engineers in each product team, and pairs per surface with the prompt engineering team at model releases.

Write and revise the prompts behind Claude's tools, features, and behaviors on a product surface; test the surface, turn findings into prompt fixes, ship them, and confirm the prompt users get is the one intended
Build the graders that prove a prompt fix and rerun on the next model; turn designers' hand-run rubrics into automated evals, then read transcripts for what the eval missed
Build visual, low-code eval tools designers can use without an engineer: assemble a comparison set from real transcripts, turn a plain-English rubric into a grader, compare prompt variants across models side by side, and read results in the tool rather than a notebook
Watch designers use those tools and make them simpler
Support model releases: test each surface against the new model, write prompt fixes and migrations, and write prompts for features launching with it, so the surface owner's call has numbers behind it
Stand up and scale the eval harness: build the test environment that exercises our 50 to 100 tools with trustworthy settings, keep evals green across models, and call whether a regression is the harness or the model
Package what prompting can't fix for training, with the eval attached: graders for crisp behaviors, human-feedback questions and good/bad pairs for fuzzy ones like writing quality

Production-quality Python
Experience building and maintaining evaluation pipelines for LLM products: graders, rubrics, comparison sets, regression suites, and the plumbing that runs them across models
Experience building internal tools with a real interface for people who do not write code
Experience standing up test harnesses, sandboxing tool calls, and pinning the settings that make runs comparable
Experience shipping prompts, or working closely with people who do, and understanding why a prompt that works on one model fails on the next
Reads transcripts, not only scores

Has worked inside a model-launch cycle
A/B testing experience and the ability to connect offline evals to online outcomes
Front-end or notebook-to-app experience, and opinions about what makes an eval result legible at a glance
Has turned product rubrics into training signal: graders, human-feedback questions, or preference pairs
Cares how Claude behaves for the people using it, not only whether the metric moved

We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.
Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains.

Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.
How we're different
We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles.

We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.
The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.
Come work with us!

About Calm
Calm is the leading mental health brand on a mission to make the world happier and healthier.

Known for its flagship consumer app—ranked #1 in its category with over 180 million downloads and availability in ten languages across 190 countries—Calm helps people sleep better, stress less, and live more mindfully through content and tools from experts and beloved celebrity voices.

Building on this foundation, Calm has created a broader portfolio including evidence-based solutions like Calm Health , offered through employers, health plans and providers, designed to expand access to mental health and sleep support, boost benefits engagement, and drive positive health outcomes.

Today, Calm supports more than 3,500 organizations and reaches over 42 million covered lives through Calm Health. Calm has been recognized as a TIME100 Most Influential Company and one of Fast Company’s Brands That Matter . Learn more at calm.com .
What We Do
At Calm we believe in making relaxation, better sleep, and mindfulness accessible to the entire world, and we hope you will help us achieve our mission. The Product & Design team is responsible for delivering Calm to our customers, ensuring that it is easy to use, supports their goals, and maintains a high level of quality across web, iOS, Android platforms.
As a Senior Product Designer on our Consumer team, you'll shape experiences used by tens of millions of people to sleep better, stress less, and live more mindfully. People often reach for Calm in their most vulnerable moments, so the craft of what we make (how it looks, moves, and feels) matters enormously.
This is a builder's role in the truest sense: you'll use AI and modern prototyping tools to move from insight to interactive prototype to shipped experience, not as a shortcut on quality, but to spend less time producing and more time on the judgment and detail that make an experience great. When anyone can generate a hundred screens in an afternoon, taste and judgment are the differentiators!
The heart of this role is balancing velocity and craft in service of making our users healthier and happier, and building intuitive, engaging and impactful experiences that drive acquisition, engagement and retention.

You'll partner closely with Product Management, Engineering, Data Science, and Marketing, and set the standard for craft across iOS, Android, and web. You will be a thought leader in design, helping to establish best practices and setting the bar for exceptional product design at Calm.

Own end-to-end product design initiatives that cover the whole product experience (visual, interaction, motion, brand integration), to create thoughtful, high-quality user-centered mobile experiences.
Prototype quickly in Figma and with AI and low-code tools like Replit, Lovable, and Claude, so you can get real, testable ideas in front of people early.
Present your design work clearly and persuasively to cross-functional stakeholders (including senior leadership), give and take feedback well, anchoring your rationale to both user needs and business goals.
Maintain strong attention to detail and collaboration through engineering implementation (build and QA) and post launch-iterations, to ensure high-quality execution.
Use data and drive research to inform the experiences you build, and leverage performance insights to evolve your approach.
Champion system-level thinking (improving how the team works and evolving Calm's design system) so the whole team works faster and smarter.
Balance multiple projects in a fast-paced environment while maintaining high standards of execution.

Experienced Product Designer: 7+ years of experience in UX and UI design with 5+ within consumer mobile and web applications.
AI-native and tooling-fluent: Highly proficient in Figma for design, and already using AI and low-code tools (Replit, Lovable, Claude) to prototype and move fast, with the judgment to know when the output is good enough and when it isn't.
Technical agility: Comfortable shipping small code changes without engineering support, bridging the gap between design and engineering by personally shipping copy and UI polish directly.
A builder: Biased toward shipping and iterating over perfect plans. You'd rather put a working prototype in front of people than write a doc about one.
Data- and research-informed: You fold both qualitative and quantitative insight into your design decisions, and you measure whether the work landed.
A strong collaborator: A low-ego, trusted partner to Product, Research, and Engineering who makes the people around them better and helps sharpen how the team works.
High craft standards: A strong advocate for accessibility, consistency, visual storytelling, brand integration, and motion design to create engaging user experiences, while still maintaining velocity.
A clear communicator: You present your thinking persuasively to stakeholders and senior leadership, give and take feedback well, and champion an experience while staying open to being wrong.

Experience with conversational or AI-native UX.
Experience working at multiple organizations, ideally including time at a consumer product in a fast-paced startup environment.
A strong portfolio demonstrating your ability to design and ship beautiful, functional, and user-friendly experiences.
Comfort shipping small copy and UI changes directly in code, without engineering support.

Why Charlie Health?

Charlie Health exists to change that. Our mission is to connect the world to life-saving behavioral health treatment. We deliver personalized, virtual care rooted in connection—between clients and clinicians, care teams, loved ones, and the communities that support them. By focusing on people with complex needs, we’re expanding access to meaningful care and driving better outcomes from the comfort of home.
As a rapidly growing organization, we're reaching more communities every day and building a team that’s redefining what behavioral health treatment can look like. If you're ready to use your skills to drive lasting change and help more people access the care they deserve, we’d love to meet you.

The people who thrive here are relentlessly curious, energized by how fast the ground is moving, crave ownership and autonomy to operate with both a high level of craft and vision-first, and operate with a true growth mindset, hungry to take on bigger challenges.

Own the seams of experience across the full Provider domain, spanning therapists, group facilitators, and clinical operations, and connect them into one coherent experience.
Advocate for and evolve a Provider Experience vision; drive alignment across engineering, product, clinical, and operations leadership, often without formal authority.
Lead the process end to end: agentic and hands-on discovery, problem definition, experience architecture, spec authorship, and building through to launch.
Build what you design. Carry work through our AI-native pipeline (prototyping, hardening, component management, spec-authorship, and swarm loops) into working, production-quality experiences.
Exercise the judgment the pipeline can't: define the problems worth solving, set the bar for quality, and know when to build with AI and when to step off it.
Lead research to uncover needs, workflow realities, and product opportunities in a clinically regulated, operations-heavy environment.
Create leverage for the team via reusable patterns, skills, tools, and standards that other designers build on and that measurably raise team velocity and quality.
Refine problem statements for others; mentor designers and raise the craft and judgment bar across the team through radically candid feedback.
Navigate extreme constraints gracefully (ambitious timelines, operational stakeholders, incomplete information) and still produce vision-level work.
Contribute to our internal design practices, ways of working, and team culture as we continue to evolve what an AI-native design org looks like.

7+ years of Product Design experience for tech/software products, preferably in Health Tech, Telehealth, or complex operational/workflow domains.
A track record of owning large, ambiguous, multi-persona problem spaces, and connecting experiences across products and surfaces rather than within a single one.
You've envisioned and delivered 0→1 experiences, and you can show how your vision work shaped organizational decisions, not just screens.
You're a systems thinker with demonstrated experience architecture skills, designing the structure of an experience, not just its surfaces.
You're an AI-native builder, fluent working with AI tools across research, prototyping, and production.
You ship working prototypes or code as a primary design output. Tool fluency is our baseline; what we're hiring for is your judgment about when and how to use it.
Deep research fluency, qualitative and quantitative, with a clear point of view on how insight earns vision the right to lead.
A strong communicator and storyteller who drives decisions with evidence and creates alignment among skeptical or constrained stakeholders.
A bias for initiative and ownership; you fill in the blanks in ambiguity and are comfortable making calls with incomplete information.
Experience contributing to token-based design systems and mentoring designers; you raise the bar for others, not just yourself.
Curiosity, adaptability, drive, and a growth mindset. You're energized by a practice that is actively reinventing itself.

Experience designing for healthcare products, EHRs, or multi-sided platforms

Ready to accelerate your career?
Clara is the fastest-growing company in Latin America. We've built the leading solution for companies to make and manage all their payments. We already help over 20,000 large and growing businesses operate with agility and financial clarity through locally issued corporate cards, bill pay, financing, and a powerful B2B platform built for scale.
Clara is backed by some of the most successful investors in the world, including top regional VCs like monashees, Kaszek, and Canary, and leading global funds like Notable Capital, Coatue, DST Global Partners, ICONIQ Growth, General Catalyst, Citi Ventures, SV Angel, Citius, Endeavor Catalyst, and Goldman Sachs - in addition to dozens of angel investors and local family offices.
We’re building the financial infrastructure that powers high-performing organizations across the region. We invite you to join us if you want to be part of a fast-paced environment that will accelerate your career and support you to do some of the best work of your life alongside a passionate and committed team distributed across the Americas.

As a Product Designer at Clara, you’ll work closely with cross-functional partners, executing design strategies that align with business goals and supporting product launches. You’ll complement your design process with AI, with the judgment to decide what to apply, when to go deep, and when to move fast and ship.

Collaborate with cross-functional partners as part of our always-on discovery pipeline to shape product requirements.
Conduct user research and testing, using AI for desk research and synthesis while owning the rigor of the insights.
Turn ambiguous problems into flows and interfaces that work for users and the business alike.
Use AI tools to go from idea to a functional, testable prototype in days, not weeks.
Ensure quality and consistency across all deliverables, including AI-assisted work, and help grow our agentic design system.
Own the UX performance of the products you design, and drive the improvements that follow.

Experience as a Product, UX, or Interaction Designer, having owned design work end to end, from discovery to shipped product, with a portfolio that shows it.
Daily, hands-on use of AI in your design workflow (Claude, Figma AI, v0, or similar), driven by real curiosity to keep pushing what it can do.
Experience in user research and usability testing, from planning and running studies to synthesizing insights that shape design decisions.
A bias for shipping, with fast iterations, early testing, and refining out in the open.
Strong attention to detail and a passion for beautiful, functional, and engaging design.
Proficiency in Figma or similar design and prototyping tools.
Clear, confident communication, comfortable presenting and defending your design decisions.
Good English level.

Frontend knowledge that helps you communicate more easily with engineering.
Comfortable with Git and the command line.
Experience with structured, agent-ready guidelines, docs built for both humans and AI to use.
A history of building your own skills, apps, or tools to make part of a process more efficient.

Clara’s Hybrid Policy
Claridians in a hybrid mode split their time between working from the office, talking to or visiting customers, or working from home. This hits a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility about how to do this in a way that makes sense for each individual and team.
We don't enforce a minimum number of days for most roles, but you're expected to spend time at the office organically, and be at the office most days during your ramp-up or when required by your leader.

Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At Coinbase , we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits.

If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” learn more about working at Coinbase .
The Design Systems team at Coinbase plays a critical role in executing on our vision to create more economic freedom for the world, and is at the center of execution for products across the entirety of the company.

Join the Design Systems team within the Consumer & Business group as a Product Designer II and shape the foundation that powers every product Coinbase ships to millions of customers. This team owns the Coinbase Design System (CDS), the single system responsible for delivering quality, consistency, and trust at scale across every experience we build.

You'll develop scalable components and patterns that help customers - from first-time crypto users to advanced traders - complete their tasks with ease and confidence, working closely with Design and Engineering across Platform and Consumer orgs to make the complex feel simple.

Own the iterative improvement of design system components and patterns, ensuring they scale across web and mobile products
Drive new system features from ideation through prototyping, user testing, and production delivery
Partner with Design and Engineering teams across the company to document, define, and evangelize scalable design patterns
Lead participation in design reviews, seeking specific feedback and incorporating relevant input to raise the quality bar
Execute on the design systems product roadmap and contribute to long-term systems strategy

3+ years of professional product design experience, including a focus specifically on design systems
Demonstrated experience designing scalable components and systems for consumer-facing web and mobile products
Proficiency with AI design tools (e.g., Figma Make, Vercel V0, Cursor) applied to systems-level work
Expert-level Figma skills including prototyping design system components within product screens
Proven track record collaborating cross-functionally with engineers, user researchers, and product teams to ship systems at scale
Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality.

Money is moving onto the internet, and the shift has a name: Open Money. This is money that is open, portable, agentic, and owned by you.

MetaMask spent the last ten years building it; with 100M+ downloads, users in ~190 countries, and trillions in cumulative transaction volume, it's the most trusted self-custodial financial platform on the internet. Now we're building the operating system for your money: one place to hold, move, grow, and use anything you own.

Join a remote-first, global team rebuilding how money works: a problem that touches everyone, every day.

MetaMask's design team is working to establish MetaMask as the premier wallet in fintech, elevating the craft of design and leading the industry as the next phase of decentralized finance unfolds. Our focus is reducing friction while preserving user trust, so more people can safely explore the world of Web3.
Prediction markets are one of the most exciting areas in consumer finance right now, sitting at the intersection of trading, sports, news, culture, and real world events. This is a big growth area for MetaMask, and we're looking for a Lead Product Designer to help shape where it goes next.

This is a chance to take real ownership of the end-to-end Prediction Markets experience inside one of the most widely used products in web3 — helping define how people discover markets, understand what's happening, trade, manage positions, and come back as events unfold.

The product is still evolving, so much of the experience is still there to be defined, and that's a big part of what makes this role interesting: we're not looking for someone to polish a finished product, we want someone who wants to help shape it.

You'll work closely with Product and Engineering, have a strong voice in what we build, and take ideas from early thinking through to something real in the hands of users.

Own the Prediction Markets experience from early thinking through launch and iteration.
Define how users discover markets, understand them, trade and manage their positions.
Make complex ideas like probabilities, liquidity and market mechanics feel clear and easy to understand.
Work closely with Product and Engineering to shape what we build, not just how it looks.
Prototype quickly using AI to explore ideas and get to stronger solutions faster.
Set a high bar for visual and interaction design, and use research and data to keep improving the product.

s.h: Would be great if you brought this to the role
s.t:
5+ years of product design experience with a strong portfolio of shipped consumer products.
You have a proven track record of delivering impactful, customer-centric designs that solve complex problems and drive commercial outcomes.
Exceptional visual and interaction design craft, with strong product instincts and attention to detail.
Experience taking complex or ambiguous problems from early ideas through to shipped experiences.
Comfortable using AI, code and modern design tools to explore, iterate and build quickly.
High ownership, strong communication and the confidence to push work forward without waiting for a perfectly defined brief.
Someone who genuinely loves sports and understands how fans follow teams, leagues, games and major sporting events.

Experience in trading, investing, fintech, sports, betting, marketplaces or other high frequency consumer products.
An interest in prediction markets and where the category could go.
Experience working with market data, probabilities, charts or financial positions.
Experience designing discovery, feeds, ranking or personalised content.
Experience with crypto or web3, although deep crypto knowledge is not required.
Don't meet all the requirements? Don't sweat it. We’re passionate about building a diverse team of humans and as such, if you think you've got what it takes for our chaotic-but-fun, remote-friendly, start-up environment—apply anyway, detailing your relevant transferable skills in your cover letter. While we have a pretty good idea of what we need, we're ready for you to challenge our thinking on who needs to be in this role .

DEPT® is a Growth Invention company built to help the world’s most ambitious brands grow faster. Operating at the intersection of technology and marketing, our 4,000+ specialists deliver growth invention services across Brand & Media, Experience, Commerce, CRM, and Technology & Data. We’re 50|50 tech and marketing, partner-led, and first to move. Clients include Google, Lufthansa, Meta, eBay, and OpenAI. We have been certified B Corp and Climate Neutral since 2021.

In this role, you’ll work with a talented team of digital designers in our growing office in Zagreb or Split, shaping top-notch experiences for international clients. You’ll collaborate with DEPT® teams across Europe, tackle complex design challenges, and push design quality to the next level.

You're not just a strong designer, you’re a people-first leader who mentors talent, challenges conventions, and helps shape a thriving team culture. From hiring to hands-on design, you'll play a key role in putting our Croatian design team on the map.

Drive creativity and deliver excellence: As a lead designer for key accounts, you set the standard for design quality and ensure that every project is not only visually appealing but also strategically sound, delivered on time, and within budget.
Strategic Collaboration: You will work closely with the UX Design Team and other leaders to further improve our capabilities and processes.

A Proven Track Record: 6+ years of experience in a same or similar role and an impressive portfolio showcasing sophisticated experience design and a deep understanding of digital platforms, ideally gained within a fast-paced agency environment.
Leadership skills: You know how to give constructive feedback and enjoy helping others grow.
Design System Nerd: You are an expert in building and maintaining scalable Design Systems that bridge the gap between aesthetics and functionality.
Accessibility as a Mindset: You view WCAG standards not as hurdles, but as fundamental design principles, effortlessly blending stunning aesthetics with inclusive usability.
Collaborative Spirit: You enjoy working in cross-functional teams, speaking the "languages" of UX Designers, Copywriters, and Developers to bring together ideas to life.
Modern Toolstack: Mastery of Figma is a must; experience with motion design and prototyping tools like Framer or Jitter is a massive plus.
Industry Pulse: You’re not only curious about digital trends, AI, new technologies, and design trends - you’re also committed to incorporating relevant innovations into your work.
Communication Skills: You are fluent in English and are able to effectively communicate complex design concepts to both executive-level clients and engineers.
The "Plus" Factor: While not a hard requirement, experience in Brand Design is a great advantage, helping us create cohesive experiences from identity to interface.
AI-Driven Design Leadership: You actively explore and implement AI-powered design tools and workflows, using them to increase team productivity, accelerate ideation and prototyping, and raise the quality of design outcomes while maintaining a strong focus on craft and human-centred design.
Trusted Client Partner: You are confident leading client engagements, facilitating workshops, presenting design rationale to senior stakeholders, and building trusted relationships that turn business challenges into impactful digital experiences.

We are a Growth Invention company built to help the world’s most ambitious brands grow faster. Operating at the intersection of technology and marketing, we create what is next by pioneering ideas, acting fast, and moving further because standing still just is not in our DNA.
We are drawn to people who stay curious, move with intent, and never stop inventing. Our culture runs on three values: better together, relentlessly curious, and get sh*t done. It is how we work, how we grow, and how we make things that matter.

Discord has a highly engaged community of millions of daily active users who use the platform for many different reasons, but there’s one thing that nearly everyone does: play video games. Discord plays a uniquely important role in the future of gaming, and we are focused on making it easier and more fun for people to hang out before, during, and after playing games.
We're looking for a Product Designer to join Growth at Discord and help shape how people find Discord, get set up, and stay connected over time.
Growth sits at the front door of our consumer org. We're responsible for how Discord shows up in the world — how new people discover us, how they land and get started, and how existing users stay close to the conversations and communities they care about. It's a broad, fast-moving surface area, and design plays a central role in making each of those moments feel unmistakably like Discord.

s.h: This role spans the full breadth of what Growth owns
s.t:
Notifications — helping users stay connected to what they care about, even when they're away. We're making notifications more intelligent, trusted, and effective: reaching people at the right moments, coordinating delivery thoughtfully, and giving users real control over their experience.
Off-platform — how Discord shows up beyond the app itself, across embeds, links, invites, web pages, and text messages. These are often someone's first impression of Discord, and there's a lot of room to make them better.
Onboarding — rethinking how new users arrive, understand what Discord is, and find their footing in those first few minutes.
GSEO — a growing effort to build the web experiences that help new people discover Discord through search in the first place.
You won't own all of this at once, but you'll work across it — and you'll help us shape how these pieces fit together into one coherent growth experience rather than a set of disconnected products.
What You'll Be Doing
Own end-to-end initiatives across Growth — a new notification type, an onboarding flow, an off-platform surface like invites or embeds, or a web experience built to bring new users in — designing across all platforms (iOS, Android, Desktop, Web)
Design with high craft and velocity — creating production-ready specs and high-fidelity prototypes while knowing when to ship vs. polish
Influence scope and strategy in partnership with your PM, engineering lead, and cross-functional teammates, balancing growth velocity with user value
Use data and research to inform decisions, partnering with research and data science teams to validate designs and understand user behavior
Think in systems — considering how discovery, onboarding, off-platform touchpoints, and re-engagement work together to create one cohesive experience
Collaborate and communicate effectively — sharing work early and often, telling compelling stories about your design rationale, and building relationships across teams
Drive projects autonomously — managing your own time and deliverables while knowing when to escalate blockers
What you should have
3+ years of product design experience designing consumer-facing digital products — though we're open to strong candidates with 2+ years who demonstrate exceptional craft and potential.
Strong visual design foundation with demonstrated aesthetic taste. You have a high level of skill crafting beautiful interfaces and an eye for creating delight in every product experience — typography, color, hierarchy, and composition are second nature to you. You're comfortable working with design systems.
Solid interaction design skills — you create intuitive flows, understand information architecture, and can design for complex, multi-step experiences. You're comfortable designing systems, not just screens.
High proficiency with Figma and prototyping tools (Protopie, Framer, Principle, etc.) — you use prototypes to communicate your vision, test concepts, and build alignment with stakeholders.
Experience shipping products collaboratively in cross-functional teams with engineering, product management, research, and data science.
Ownership mindset with a bias toward action — you proactively drive projects and decisions forward. You help guide product vision through design explorations, documentation, and presentations.

Personal use of Discord and passion for gaming or community platforms
Experience designing growth, onboarding, acquisition, or lifecycle products
Understanding of how products reach and grow users across surfaces — notifications, messaging, web, SEO, or shareable/viral loops
Familiarity with experimentation frameworks and data-driven iteration

Our mission at Duolingo is to develop the best education in the world and make it universally available. But we’ve got more left to do — and that’s where you come in!
Duolingo is the world's most popular learning app. Beyond our core learning product, we also offer English proficiency testing with the Duolingo English Test, and are bringing new subjects into the Duolingo app, where people can develop their Math and Music skills.
We are passionate about educating our users, making fact-based decisions, and finding innovative solutions to complex problems. We offer meaningful work, limitless learning opportunities, and collaboration with world-class minds. Come brighten your life and over half a billion more!’

This role reports to the Director of Product Design on Monetization. Monetization is the revenue engine that powers our company. Our teams focus on unlocking value for users through subscriptions, ads and in-app purchases. As a Staff Designer, you’ll play a key role in defining how users experience that value, from their first touchpoint to being long-term loyal users.
As a member of the Duolingo Design team, this role is an instrumental creative partner in key monetization vectors at Duolingo—from our delightful purchase flow to our seasonal avatar events. At Duolingo, we take pride in and agonize over crafting a user-friendly (and fun) experience for everyone.

s.h: Will you join us on our mission?
s.t:
🧠You will...
Define and evolve both the free and paid user experiences across Monetization surfaces within the Duolingo language app
Play a leadership role on the Monetization design team in shaping our product roadmap and product development
Partner with engineers and product managers to define both the long-term strategy and the short-term tactics for our products
Work collaboratively with designers and artists to build upon and expand the Duolingo design language
Sometimes work on very broadly defined, loose concepts, and sometimes on narrowly defined, tactical features
Consider all parts when crafting the experience: from copy to animation to business impact
✅You have...
An online portfolio with consumer mobile app or web design samples
Design experience in a consumer application, product, or software role
A desire to strive for excellence in your work until all details are attended to
The ability to explain your work, process, and decisions and seek feedback to help you produce your best work
⭐️Outstanding candidates will have...
Experience designing for fast-paced Monetization, Growth or subscription-based products
Experience with strong experimentation culture and iterative improvements
An interest in developing design talent and improving design craft

Figma is growing our team of passionate creatives and builders on a mission to make design accessible to all. Figma’s platform helps teams bring ideas to life—whether you're brainstorming, creating a prototype, translating designs into code, or iterating with AI. From idea to product, Figma empowers teams to streamline workflows, move faster, and work together in real time from anywhere in the world. If you're excited to shape the future of design and collaboration, join us!
We're looking for a technically-minded product designer who is excited to shape how design, code, and AI-powered workflows come together at Figma.

In this role, you'll improve how Figma understands production code and design systems, design workflows that move from design to code and back again, and extend Figma's agentic capabilities into developer tools and the places teams already work.

You'll turn ambiguity into clarity alongside engineers, PMs, and researchers, bringing simplicity and craft to complex technical problems as we help define the future of how software is made.
This is a full-time role that can be held from our London hub or remotely within the UK.

Shape and prototype new workflows that bring design and production code closer together, including AI-powered experiences that connect Figma with the tools teams already use to build
Contribute to overall strategy and decision-making about product direction
Help deliver and refine clear storytelling around product needs and opportunities
Work cross-functionally with product management, engineering, UX writing, data science, and research peers
Create and iterate on flows, prototypes, and high-fidelity visuals, as well as provide thoughtful feedback for others doing the same so you can all do your best work
Design and ship high-quality features and product improvements in Figma's core product surfaces
Contribute to our design org's culture by participating in design critiques, mentoring peers, and sharing best practices across teams

s.h: We'd love to hear from you if you have
s.t:
3+ years of experience designing UX and UI for software products of similar scale and complexity
Strong visual craft and attention to detail across composition, typography, layout, interaction design, and prototyping
Proven ability to independently drive end-to-end design processes from discovery through launch, balancing user needs, technical constraints, and business goals
Ability to guide decision-making through structured thinking, clear design rationale, and user-centered research
Experience designing technically complex products, ideally developer tools or extensible platforms, with an understanding of software development workflows, APIs, and systems; experience prototyping and evaluating AI-powered or nondeterministic interactions is a plus

s.h: While it's not required, it's an added plus if you also have
s.t:
Familiarity with web technologies like HTML/CSS, AI coding tools such as Codex, Cursor, or Claude Code
A strong understanding of advanced Figma features like Auto Layout, Variables, and Components
Hands-on experience building with web technologies, APIs, CLIs, MCP, model evals, or other tools used to create developer and AI products
A history of working on canvas-based interfaces or tools that support creative workflows
Prior work involving design systems, like creating, maintaining, or contributing to a design system
At Figma, one of our values is Grow as you go. We believe in hiring smart, curious people who are excited to learn and develop their skills. s.h: About the Role: What's in the Box
s.t:
HelloFresh Group is building the next generation of consumer experiences across its portfolio—from discovery and personalization to shopping and subscription management. The Consumer UX team is at the heart of this work, designing end-to-end experiences that are simple, delightful, and grounded in real customer needs.
Services are required for Senior UX Designers across two squad contexts: one embedded in Good Chop , the premium American meat and seafood subscription brand, and one in the central Consumer UX team working across the broader HelloFresh Group portfolio. Both roles share the same craft bar, strategic expectations, and ways of working.
These are full-accountability roles inside a fast-paced environment. The provider will partner with Product and Engineering leads on a cross-functional squad, where UX serves as a strategic input to shape direction from the start. This role does not include people management responsibilities.

Consumer Experience Design: Lead design from concept to shipped product, maintaining full accountability for the consumer experience across touchpoints while holding a high quality bar at every stage.
Strategy and Roadmap Influence: Frame problem spaces before briefs are created. Bring evidence-backed consumer insights into squad planning to surface opportunities and inform what gets built.
Craft and Execution: Maintain a high personal standard across UI, interaction design, motion, micro-interaction, and UX writing, using animation and motion as intentional strategic tools.
AI-Native Workflow: Utilize AI across the entire design lifecycle—including insight synthesis, discovery, rapid prototyping, and design-to-code workflows—to increase execution speed and precision.

Experience: 6+ years in product design, with a proven track record delivering high-quality consumer products end-to-end.
Consumer Instinct: Deep understanding of consumer-facing products and decision-making drivers across the full customer lifecycle. Subscription domain experience is a plus.
Strategic Range: Ability to define problem spaces before designing solutions, utilizing evidence to refine project scopes and contribute to roadmap strategies.
Craft Mastery: Exceptional visual and interaction design skills with deep focus on hierarchy, motion, micro-interaction, and animation. High proficiency in Figma and strong familiarity with front-end technical constraints.
High Agency: Proactivity to advocate for optimal design solutions, bringing conviction to decisions and collaborating effectively with cross-functional partners.
Research Fluency: Ability to frame research questions, run lightweight studies, and translate findings into design direction.
AI-Native in Practice: Active use of AI tools (such as Figma AI and Claude) in live project workflows for synthesis, discovery, prototyping, and code generation.
Communication: Clear presentation capabilities, skill in facilitating cross-functional alignment, and the ability to defend design decisions using data and evidence.

Global collaboration at scale: Collaborate with experienced engineers and product partners across HelloTech’s international teams, in a culture of active knowledge sharing.
Technology with real-world impact: Build and operate modern systems at global scale, supporting millions of customers and complex supply chain operations.
Technical/Product/Design leadership: Drive best practices and influence design quality, architecture, and ways of working in an autonomous, product-led setup.
End-to-end development/delivery: Drive decisions from problem definition to production, improving systems and enabling long-term scalability.
Access to workspace at Warsaw Centre Point: The hub offers modern facilities including showers, breakout zones, outdoor space, cycle parking, and refreshments (coffee, soft drinks, and fruit).

Shape product direction

Connect customer needs, behavioural insights, commercial goals, and emerging technology to develop strong product directions.

Apply strong design judgment to AI-generated outputs, understanding when AI accelerates quality and when human craft, intuition, and critical thinking matter most.
Raise the bar for design craft

Identify opportunities to improve the quality and coherence of the Growth experiences you work on.
Contribute patterns, practices, and examples that help other designers deliver stronger work.
Give and seek thoughtful critique, using feedback to continuously strengthen the work.

A strong portfolio demonstrating end-to-end ownership of complex consumer experiences, from understanding the problem through shipped outcomes and learning.
Experience independently navigating ambiguous problems, making sound design decisions, and influencing product direction within your area.
Growth and experimentation expertise
Strong experience designing B2C growth, e-commerce, subscription, marketplace, or other transaction-driven experiences.
You understand experimentation deeply and can translate behavioural data, customer insights, and business metrics into meaningful design opportunities.
You know how to optimize for conversion without losing sight of trust, comprehension, customer value, and longer-term engagement.
Exceptional product design craft
Strong expertise across interaction and visual design, including hierarchy, information architecture, responsive behaviour, motion, and micro-interactions.
You can take complex experiences and make them feel simple, and can articulate what separates a functional experience from a great one.
You care about the details while understanding when speed, learning, and iteration matter more than perfection.
AI-native design fluency
AI is already part of how you work, not something you are waiting to adopt.
You regularly use AI across multiple stages of your design process, whether that’s discovery, synthesis, ideation, prototyping, or execution.
You’re comfortable experimenting with tools such as Figma AI, Claude, Claude Code, Gemini, or similar emerging technologies.
You’re interested not only in using AI to work faster, but in understanding how it changes what we can design for customers.
Systems thinking
You naturally look beyond the individual screen or experiment to understand how experiences connect.

At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive.
Lyft Urban Solutions powers the bike-sharing and scooter-sharing systems that move millions of people in over 60 cities worldwide. We built North America's first automated bike-share system and continue to lead the micromobility revolution.

Our systems operate globally - from Citi Bike in New York to BIXI in Montreal, Divvy in Chicago, Capital Bikeshare in DC, and iconic systems in Austin, Barcelona, Bogota, Boston, Buenos Aires, Columbus, Detroit, Dubai, London, Madrid, Mexico City, Monaco, Pittsburgh, Portland, Rio de Janeiro, San Francisco, Toronto, and beyond.

Ready to shape how millions of people move through their cities every day?
We are looking for a passionate Product Designer to join our Montreal office to work on Lyft’s micromobility Operations Technology team.
As a member of the Operations Technology team, you’ll be responsible for evolving the platform that drives the global on-the-ground operations of our business. You’ll be designing features that are used in warehouses, vans, & on-the-ground to make our transportation systems some of the most reliable in the world. You’ll confront complex technical challenges & advocate for experiences that delight our operators and promote efficiency.
Our Montreal office developed the first automated bikes-share system in North America and continues to work on the platform today that provides state-of-the-art electric bikes and scooters for tens of millions of rides per year.
As a product designer at Lyft, you will be involved at every step of product development, from brainstorming broad ideas to ensuring design quality through launch. Using your full range of interaction, visual, and product thinking skills. As a product designer on the Lyft Urban Solutions team you will own the design of features within the core rider experience for our bike and scooter riders, within the Lyft app and our market specific apps.
In a lot of ways, we function as a startup, meaning we all work closely and collaboratively across organizations to align on product vision and ship products. Our Design and Research teams live and breathe a user-centered process to create the best possible, end-to-end, experience for riders all over the world. We can be scrappy when we need to be, though we are always focused on quality and influence.
As a qualified candidate, you have a track record of leading projects to successful outcomes for users and the business. You are a strong cross-functional partner, a great communicator, and are able to take a solution from idea to implementation. You uphold a high-quality bar and have a strong appreciation for the details. Above all, you approach problems holistically and create elegantly simple solutions to multi-faceted problems.

Plan strategically and think tactically as a partner with product and engineering to define the future of the team.

Lead the design of complex AI-powered interactions in your product cluster, accounting for trust, transparency, fallback states, and human-in-the-loop considerations
Embrace the use of modern AI-based tools like Claude, Figma Make, Cursor, Vercel, Loveable or equivalent not as theatre, but as a meaningful multiplier to your workflow.
Partner with our UX research team to lead interviews, usability tests, and competitive analysis and translate findings into clear product direction and guidance
Develop presentations, wireframes, mockups, and prototypes that effectively communicate interaction and design intent across web and mobile surfaces.
Partner with PMs to shape requirements and with engineers to protect design intent through delivery
Contribute to Showpad's design systems — adding components, documenting patterns, raising consistency across product areas
Communicate design rationale through strategic storytelling: you can walk a PM, an engineer, and a senior stakeholder through the same decision and each one gets what they need
Establish scalable AI-assisted workflows for your own work — research synthesis, rapid prototyping, concept generation — and help others on the team use them effectively

You have 5+ years of product design experience and a portfolio of shipped enterprise or B2B SaaS work. You take full ownership of complex, ambiguous problem spaces and deliver strong work without needing the brief handed to you. You think in systems — considering how an isolated design decision ripples across the broader product — and you contribute meaningfully to the design system, not just consume it.

Staff Product Designer, Commercial Growth
Squarespace's Commercial Growth organization brings together the product, engineering, and strategy teams responsible for how Squarespace builds, prices, and grows its business across every product line. Within that org, the Commercial Product team owns the customer-facing experiences that drive purchase, adoption, and expansion — from the moment a prospective customer discovers Squarespace to the point they convert, upgrade, and grow.
We're looking for a Staff Product Designer to own the end-to-end commercial experience across cart, checkout, cross-sell, and pricing pages.

This is a high-leverage, high-visibility role at the intersection of monetization strategy and product craft — translating pricing, packaging, and bundling goals into scalable, intuitive user experiences that work across Squarespace's full product portfolio. This is a Player–Coach individual contributor role at the Staff level.

You'll bring deep systems thinking and exceptional craft to some of the most commercially consequential surfaces in the product, while also serving as a force multiplier for the broader Commercial Growth design community. This role reports to the Director of GTM Product Design.
This is the right role for a senior designer who understands that commercial UX is not just a conversion problem — it's a systems problem. If you can hold the full arc from Frontsite discovery through post-purchase expansion, think in merchandising patterns and interaction models rather than one-off flows, and partner credibly with product, engineering, and revenue systems counterparts, this role is built for you.
You’ll Get To…
Own the Commercial Product Design Surface: Lead design across plan selection, cart merchandising, and cross-sell — creating cohesive, intentional experiences across the full commercial ecosystem rather than isolated flows.
Translate Monetization Strategy into Scalable UX: Work closely with Commercial Strategy to translate pricing, packaging, bundling, discounting, and messaging requirements into flexible, reusable design patterns that hold up across products and offers.
Design Cross-Sell and Merchandising Systems: Develop cross-sell placements, supporting assets, and interaction models tied to targeting strategy — designing for flexibility so that what works for one product line can scale across others.
Partner Across Product, Engineering, and RevSys: Collaborate closely with product and engineering leaders on customer-facing purchase and conversion flows, and work with RevSys counterparts where commercial product experiences depend on shared systems or implementation constraints.
Connect Frontsite to Downstream Conversion: Extend design thinking across Frontsite-connected journeys so that discovery and downstream conversion feel intentional and connected — not like separate experiences owned by separate teams.
Partner with Platform and Data Science on Targeting and Experimentation: Work alongside Platform and Data Science teams when targeting logic or experimentation affects the user experience, ensuring that personalization and testing are designed with the customer journey in mind.
Establish Design Consistency Across Commercial Growth: Help raise the design bar across the newly unified Commercial Growth organization — establishing patterns, principles, and standards that create coherence across a complex, multi-surface ecosystem.
Mentor and Elevate Craft: Serve as a craft mentor across Commercial Growth design as we expand — giving sharp, actionable feedback, pairing with designers on complex systems problems, and raising the quality bar for both systems thinking and visual and interaction design.

10+ years of experience in product design at a digital product company, including time operating at a Staff or equivalent level.
A portfolio demonstrating complex, systems-level work — ideally across commerce, checkout, pricing, or monetization surfaces — with clear impact on user and business outcomes.
Experience leading cross-functional workstreams from ambiguity to shipped product, including setting direction, defining milestones, and aligning stakeholders across product, engineering, and data teams.
A track record of translating business and monetization requirements — pricing, packaging, discounting, merchandising — into scalable, intuitive UX patterns that work across a broad product portfolio.
Strong systems thinking: you architect experiences that feel simple by mapping data models, flows, and dependencies across multiple product areas.
High-agency operator who can create momentum without fully defined requirements — you impose structure on ambiguous problems by framing the space, surfacing constraints, and clarifying goals for others.
Experience designing for or alongside experimentation and targeting systems, with an understanding of how personalization and A/B logic affect the user experience.
Exceptional communication and storytelling skills — you can zoom from high-level strategy to concrete UX decisions with clarity, and you're comfortable representing design rationale to senior leadership and cross-functional stakeholders.
You lead by example, setting a craft and systems bar that other designers actively look to emulate, and you enjoy coaching designers at different levels.
Experience working on Frontsite or marketing-site-connected journeys, with an understanding of how discovery and conversion relate across the funnel, is a strong plus.

Flex is a growth-stage, NYC headquartered FinTech company that is creating the best rent payment experience. Our mission is to empower as many renters as possible with flexibility over their most significant recurring expense. After deliberately keeping a stealth profile as we built up unprecedented investor support and an enthusiastic user base, we are looking for motivated individuals to help us keep our mission growing. Will you be a part of the team?

As a Principal Product Designer at Flex, you’ll solve problems for consumers across the country who are underserved by existing financial products. We’re handling people’s most significant recurring expense, which means the stakes of getting the experience right are real: a confusing screen or a poorly handled edge case can cost someone a late fee, a credit mark, or a difficult conversation with their leasing office.
We’re looking for a designer to lead a full area of our business. This is an individual contributor role with the influence of a leader. Your leverage comes from the artifacts you make, the standards you set, and the designers you make better, not from a reporting line. You’ll still be deep in the work leading design exploration on the most critical projects, and building the prototypes that show where a body of work is headed and what it will unlock.
This is a highly measured, highly cross-functional environment, with a big opportunity for designers to bridge true customer needs with creative solutions. You’ll work alongside product managers, engineers, data analysts, risk, and compliance partners, and most of what you design will run as an experiment before it becomes the default.

The designers who do their best work here are highly creative with solutioning, curious about the numbers, comfortable with constraints, and willing to change their minds when the evidence says to. All of your design skills will be put to use, from design thinking to interaction design and visual design.

Product Designer
In the 1960s, the Italian artist and inventor Bruno Munari was studying spontaneous forms: shapes that emerge from the interaction of material, function, and environment.
When Danese Milano commissioned him to design a lamp that was practical, durable, affordable, and easy to transport, Munari was reminded of the traditional rice paper lanterns he had encountered when traveling in Japan. But rice paper lanterns are fragile, hard to clean, and tend to yellow over time.
Looking for an industrial alternative, he discovered filanca—a synthetic stretch nylon used exclusively for women's stockings at the time.
Munari visited hosiery factories to test the material and see what forms it could take. "We do not make lamps, sir. Only stockings," one factory told him. Munari replied, "You'll see."
The result was the Falkland lamp: only a few centimeters thick when packaged, as tall as a human when hung, its spontaneous form emerging from the elasticity of the nylon and metal rings of different diameters inserted at regular intervals, enlarged by gravity when suspended from above.
Munari didn't begin with the form of a lamp. He began with the qualities it needed, then looked outside the conventions of lighting to find the right materials and methods. We're looking for a designer who works the same way: someone who studies the systems and materials at hand, then finds a way of putting them together that feels both unexpected and inevitable.
At Co–Star, the materials are a 4,000-year-old system of astrology, planetary data from NASA, and a corpus written by astrologers and poets. The qualities we're designing for: astrology made accessible without asking anyone to learn a complex system, and a language that lets people share something intimate with their friends.
We're hiring a Senior Product Designer to continue cultivating those qualities across Co–Star and new experiments. You'll move between product architecture, interaction design, prototyping, and visual design. Ideas rarely arrive as polished specs. You'll help decide what we make next and how it works.

Design and build products from concept through launch.
Work closely with design and engineering on new features and launches.
You care about the details—typography, layout, motion, responsiveness, loading states, and performance—that make an experience great.
Contribute visual assets for marketing.
Prototype ideas quickly using Figma, Claude, Cursor, and whatever tools helps move the work forward.

You have 2–5 years of experience designing and building for the web.
You move fluidly across the full design process, from early concept through final production.
You have an instinct for the details that make interfaces feel considered: type, spacing, motion, and how they all work together.
You know enough HTML and CSS to work effectively with engineers—or to build parts of the experience yourself.
